harness_surface.guardrails: CLAUDE.md (What this agent does not do) + .claude/settings.json deny
harness_surface.skills: skills/<id>@v<n>/ (SKILL.md, skill.json, scripts/, cases.json), run through src/run_skill.py
harness_surface.session_skills: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md: run-skill, the one that names the runner, with library/index.md and one page per library skill beside it, rendered from the manifests; classify-knowledge; choose-session-level

note: A build copies this tree, fills CLAUDE.md's placeholders, adds tools/<name>/ with adapter.py, tool.json and errors/, fills CAPABILITIES.json and envelope/, writes validation/ and replay/ tasks, copies the skills the specification names into skills/ unchanged, renders .claude/skills/run-skill/library/ from their manifests (index.md and one page per skill) and writes .claude/agents/<name>.md for the subagents it names. The diff from this tree is recorded next to the bundle. v2 added src/run_skill.py and the Subagents section to v1 (meta_agent/tasks/010). v3 adds three session skills (meta_agent/tasks/015; the person, 2026-11-12): run-skill, which sends the bundle's session to src/run_skill.py and says what a session may and may not change, with its library pages; classify-knowledge and choose-session-level, adapted to a bundle from the Meta-Agent's own, naming no path outside the bundle and no script under src/; and in CLAUDE.md the sentences that name them and the rules they repeat. Bundle check B15 judges a bundle of v3 or later. v4 changes text only, after a fresh session was watched in a bundle of v3 (meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261112-meta-macbook-20261112-1-5.json): run-skill also says how a tool that no library skill calls is called, through src/run_tool.py, and its description and CLAUDE.md's sentence for it say so; tasks/001-start.md says that src/validate_tasks.py ends with a failure status when the verdict is undecided and that this is expected; a build with no library skill writes 'no library skill' where it wrote 'no skills'. v5 changes text only, after a fresh session was watched in a copy of a bundle of v4 outside the repository (meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261113-meta-macbook-20261112-1-1.json, answered in meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261113-design-macbook-20261112-1-1.json): tasks/001-start.md covers a scientific verdict of not_run as well as undecided; CLAUDE.md says that envelope/safety.json holds one entry per safety value and that a file with none means no tool requires a gate, that the folder named runs is made by the session when it first writes there, and that an input nothing in the bundle gives is one line in failures.jsonl like a missing skill; run-skill has a section for such an input. v6 changes text and no script, after two fresh sessions worked in copies of bundles of v5 in a test run outside the repository (meta_agent/tasks/016; meta_agent/inbox/seats/20261116-design-macbook-20261116-1-2.json): CLAUDE.md names README.md, TEMPLATE.json and CAPABILITIES.json and says what a claim with not_here is; it says that the runner of skills writes a record only with --record and that the runner of tools writes none, what the status each runner and each check ends with means, that the three checks are not tool calls, that a replay item made by hand is still compared by src/replay.py, and which keys a line of failures.jsonl has; and it says that a grade is the builder's and is not derived here. The bundle carries no grade table: deriving a grade is a calculation, a calculation in a bundle is a library skill, and the library has none for it, so a table without the skill would be read by hand. run-skill repeats the procedure for a record, for a kept output and for a replay item. From this version the builder writes the unit a tool contract names into the Tools section, writes CAPABILITIES.json with the name of the document it read and not its path in the builder's tree, marks a claim that names a tool the bundle does not carry, and lists what is held. Bundle check B16 judges a bundle of this version or later. Every earlier version stays under templates/.
